title: Leap Year Checker
description: Determine if a year is a leap year using the full Gregorian calendar rules.

steps.title: Divisible by 4
steps.description: Write an `isLeapYear` function that returns `true` if a year is divisible by 4 using the modulo operator.
hints: A year is divisible by 4 if year % 4 === 0
Return true if divisible by 4, false otherwise

verification.successMessage: 2024 is a leap year, 2023 is not!
verification.failureMessage: isLeapYear(2024) should be true, isLeapYear(2023) should be false.

steps.title: Full leap year rules
steps.description: Implement the complete Gregorian leap year rules: divisible by 400 = true, divisible by 100 = false, divisible by 4 = true.

verification.successMessage: 2000 is leap, 1900 is not, 2024 is leap — correct rules!
verification.failureMessage: 2000 (div by 400) = true, 1900 (div by 100 not 400) = false, 2024 (div by 4) = true.

steps.title: Test years in a range
steps.description: Write a function that prints all leap years in a given range (e.g., 2000 to 2024) using a loop.
hints: Print the year if it's a leap year

verification.successMessage: Leap years from 2000 to 2024 listed correctly!

steps.title: Count leap years
steps.description: Write a `countLeapYears` function that returns the number of leap years between two years.
hints: Use the same loop approach but count instead of printing
Increment a counter each time you find a leap year

steps.title: Find the next leap year
steps.description: Write a `nextLeapYear` function that finds the next leap year after a given year.
hints: Start from year + 1 and check each year
Use a while loop that continues until you find a leap year
Return the first leap year you find

verification.successMessage: Next leap year after 2023 is 2024, after 2024 is 2028!
verification.failureMessage: nextLeapYear(2023) should be 2024, nextLeapYear(2024) should be 2028.
